name: The One Ring
oracle_text:
Indestructible
When The One Ring enters, if you cast it, you gain protection from everything until your next turn.
At the beginning of your upkeep, you lose 1 life for each burden counter on The One Ring.
{T}: Put a burden counter on The One Ring, then draw a card for each burden counter on The One Ring.
blocked_sentences: When The One Ring enters, if you cast it, you gain protection from everything until your next turn.

needs.what: grant_protection must be able to name a *player* as the recipient (a `player` spec beside `objects`), to grant the quality "everything" rather than only a list of colours/types/subtypes, and to last `until_your_next_turn` instead of only until end of turn -- and every rule that reads protection (targeting, damage, enchanting, blocking) has to consult a player's protection set, not just an object's
needs.why_existing_wont_do: grant_protection resolves its recipients through choose_objects and then skips any oid that is not `on_battlefield`, so a player can never receive it; its qualities are built only from `from_colors` (each entry loader-validated against KNOWN_COLORS), `from_types` and `from_subtypes`, none of which can express "everything"; and it writes an `until_eot` TempEffect that cleanup ends this turn, so the "until your next turn" clock does not exist for it. `characteristics.protection_from(state, oid)` is object-keyed throughout, so there is no player-side reader either. The `protection` static_effect has the same three limits and is a printed static on a permanent besides, not something a self_enters trigger can install. `grant_keyword` is not a substitute: protection is parameterised and a Keyword is a bare string.
